Feedback can change what a system remembers and foregrounds, not only a visible reputation score. Relevance decay and changes to a memory graph should remain inspectable so that adaptation does not silently erase inconvenient evidence. DP22 governs continuity and accountable resurfacing.

Failure

changes.afterText:
Reporting channels should offer anonymous AI-interaction risk flags for people who cannot safely identify themselves, with a confidential follow-up route where feasible. Reporters should receive status updates, and communities should be able to inspect anonymized outcome information where safe. Reporting privacy and visible follow-through must coexist with safeguards against weaponized reports.

Failure
changes.rationale: Combines whistleblower reporting and outcome-update proposals without duplicating the existing reporting workflow.

The proposal does not establish validity, a usable measure, or a credible path from inferred traits to fairer opportunities; the privacy and exclusion risks are material to the claimed benefit.
